newsitem.title: UK: LASMO says Iona North Sea field starts production.
newsitem.headline: LASMO says Iona North Sea field starts production.

text.p: LASMO said on Thursday production at the Elf-operated Iona oilfield in the central North Sea began on January 21 at a test rate of 4,400 barrels per day (bpd).
LASMO North Sea holds 20 percent of the field while Elf Exploration UK, a subsidiary of French oil giant Elf Aquitaine, has a 24.333 percent stake.
Other partners are Texaco Britain Ltd (23.5 percent), Union Texas Petroleum (20 percent) and Enterprise Oil (12.167 percent).
LASMO said test results showed well productivity was higher than expected.
"There will be a series of reservoir tests over the next few months and we expect final production rates to rise above this initial level," said David Thomas, central North Sea manager for LASMO.
Industry analysts estimate the field's recoverable reserves at a modest seven million barrels of oil and three billion cubic feet of gas.
Iona, formerly known as South Piper, is situated in block 15/17 some five kilometres south of the 50,000 bpd Piper field.
It is being developed using deviated wells from the nearby Saltire A platform, and will export oil via the Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands off the northeast coast of Scotland.
